transcript: I used to be so stressed by payday because I would use this month's salary to pay off last month's credit card Bill. Not anymore. Now it's my favourite day of the month. And here's exactly what I do to stay in control of my spending. Black coffee injected in my veins. I've said it approximately a million times before, but you need to pay yourself first. That is the smallest shift with the biggest impact. And future you will be insanely grateful for this. In this month I put £1,366 in my stocks and shares ISA and £300 in my cash ISA for emergencies. As always, £1,800 is going straight into my pension. Next we have fixed costs. Every month I put away £1,500 and that is less than 30% of m…[omitted — see transcript_note]…ed on £30,000 in 2018. At that time, I was still nannying on the weekends and all the money I made from nannying went straight into investments or into paying off debt. And I continue doing that for I think another one or two years. And then now for the past year, I've been posting on social media. I'm making serious money. I've not touched any of that money yet. And I'm planning on putting it all in my pensions so that I can achieve my goal of hitting 1 million before I turn 40. And No. 3 is living below your means.
